A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show the importance of adversarial learning for variational inference and we demonstrate its utility for inferring spiking activity from calcium imaging.
adversarial training of latent variable models can be used to improve the performance and robustness of posterior sampling.

The main takeaway from our work is that

importance weighting methods are a promising direction for adversarially trained generative models, particularly in the context of challenging inference problems in which approximate posteriors cannot be directly evaluated.
adversarial training can be used to improve training and inference in generative models with intractable likelihoods and inference.
the adversarial training of importance weighted variational inference can be a useful alternative to standard variational methods in latent variable models.
